passage: When a young company issues new shares to raise money, its founders keep every share they already held. Yet each of those shares now stands for a smaller fraction of the company, because the company has more owners than before, so a founder who once controlled half the votes may lose her majority. Economists therefore say that a new issue ______ the founders' stake, even in cases where the company's total value rises.
prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation: The word "dilutes" fits because the founders keep all their shares while each share becomes a smaller fraction of a company with more owners, so their proportional stake weakens. "Depletes" fails because nothing is used up: the founders still hold every share they had. "Devalues" fails because the passage allows the company's total value to rise, so the stake's worth need not fall; the loss is in proportion, not price. "Encumbers" fails because no debt or legal claim is placed on the founders' shares.
